findings.claim: WaitsForHop treats any non-builder, non-delivery role as a chain waiting for a hop, including an empty or unknown v.Role when Records > 0. Such a view would get the hop remedy (append a hop) instead of the open remedy. The allow/deny decision is unchanged, so this only affects the denial text, and it is not reachable with a verified chain. The tests do not cover an empty role.

evidence: Read engine/oddtask/app/guard.go CheckLaunch. The new WaitsForHop branch only chooses between HopMessage and deny(reason) inside the existing DecideWorkflow non-empty branch. Allow and deny are unchanged, and an allow still returns an empty string.
Read DecideWorkflow in engine/oddtask/workflow.go. The role check is the last case, so WaitsForHop (which sets Role to builder and re-runs it) is true only when the role is the sole failing reason.
Read WorkflowMessage and guardPrefix in the worktree to compare the message format.
Not run: no tests or commands were executed.

Tests added in the diff cover the exact HopMessage text, the role matrix of WaitsForHop (builder and delivery false, earlier failures false), the CheckLaunch hop and delivery paths, the next-subtask allow after a reviewer-to-builder hop, and the three docs.
